Here's the result of running `cat -n` on /tmp/gestalt/phase/3350baf6-9bd5-4cac-b688-f263972317f9/7/AGENTS.md:
     1	# AGENTS.md — trackeros
     2	
     3	This file is the primary agent orientation document for this project.
     4	Read this file completely before taking any action.
     5	
     6	## What this project is
     7	
     8	Trackeros — a corporate operations web and mobile platform for
     9	  mid-sized companies. Provides employee self-service (leave
    10	  requests, balances, expense claims), manager workflows
    11	  (approvals, team views, time-off calendars), and HR admin
    12	  surfaces (leave policy configuration, balance accruals,
    13	  audit reports).
    14	  
    15	  Backend: TypeScript on Node 20 (Fastify), PostgreSQL via
    16	  Knex migrations + a thin repository layer, BullMQ for
    17	  background jobs (accrual schedulers, notification fanout).
    18	  Module structure: src/modules/<name>/<name>.{model,
    19	  repository,service,controller,routes}.ts. Domain modules
    20	  include leave, balance, employee, policy, notification.
    21	  Shared utilities under src/shared/ (db connection, base
    22	  repository, error types).
    23	  
    24	  Frontend: React + Vite SPA for the web client, React Native
    25	  for the mobile client (shared @trackeros/contracts package
    26	  for the typed REST surface). Auth via JWT against the
    27	  backend's /auth endpoints; identity comes from corporate
    28	  OIDC in production and from local users in development.
    29	  
    30	  Tests: Jest for unit + integration. CI on GitHub Actions
    31	  runs lint (ESLint) + typecheck (tsc --noEmit) + unit tests +
    32	  a Semgrep security pass on every PR. Conventional Commits +
    33	  squash-merge. Strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict
    34	  null checks).
    35	
    36	## Project stack
    37	
    38	- Runtime: Node 20 LTS
    39	- Package manager: npm
    40	- Test framework: Jest
    41	- Backend: Fastify
    42	- Frontend: React Native
    43	- Database: PostgreSQL
    44	
    45	See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full architecture overview and
    46	module layout.
    47	
    48	Note: the Gestalt platform itself runs on Node 20 + pnpm 9.x as a
    49	self-imposed constraint. That has no bearing on this project —
    50	user projects use whatever stack matches their description.
    51	
    52	## Architecture rules
    53	
    54	1. Modules never import from each other's internals — only from index.ts
    55	2. All database access through the repository pattern (GP-001)
    56	3. Every state-changing operation produces an audit record (GP-002)
    57	4. RBAC enforced at middleware, never inline (GP-005)
    58	
    59	## What agents must never do
    60	
    61	- Violate principle GP-003 as defined in `GOLDEN_PRINCIPLES.md`.
    62	- Violate principle GP-004 as defined in `GOLDEN_PRINCIPLES.md`.
    63	- Violate principle GP-005 as defined in `GOLDEN_PRINCIPLES.md`.
    64	- Violate principle GP-006 as defined in `GOLDEN_PRINCIPLES.md`.
    65	
    66	## When context is missing
    67	
    68	Emit a `CONTEXT_GAP` signal with the specific missing information identified.
    69	
    70	## Operator notes — Git credential scopes
    71	
    72	The personal access token registered with this project drives BOTH the
    73	platform's clone/push and the deploy layer's CI/CD calls. Required scopes:
    74	
    75	- **GitHub PAT (classic)** — `repo` (clone, push, create PRs) +
    76	  `workflow` (dispatch GitHub Actions workflows). Fine-grained PATs need
    77	  Contents: read+write, Pull requests: read+write, Actions: read+write,
    78	  Workflows: read+write.
    79	- **GitLab Project Access Token** — `api` + `write_repository`.
    80	- **Azure DevOps PAT** — `Code (Read & Write)` + `Build (Read & Execute)`.
    81	
    82	Without the workflow scope the deploy layer's pipeline-agent will fail with
    83	a `GOLDEN_PRINCIPLE_BREACH` signal and the intent will be escalated for
    84	human review. Re-issue the PAT with the missing scope and re-register the
    85	project to recover.
    86	
    87	## Custom agents
    88	
    89	Project-specific agents can be defined in `agents.yaml` under
    90	`custom_agents`. They run after the framework generate agents
    91	(intent / design / context / lint-config / code / test) and BEFORE
    92	dispatch to the quality gate. Each custom agent receives the
    93	generated artifacts as part of its prompt and returns structured
    94	findings.
    95	
    96	The orchestrator routes findings to typed signals the gate
    97	evaluates:
    98	
    99	- `high` severity findings → `CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION`
   100	- `medium` / `low` findings → `LINT_FAILURE`
   101	- LLM error or response parse failure → `CONTEXT_GAP`
   102	
   103	Custom agents **never** emit `GOLDEN_PRINCIPLE_BREACH` — that
   104	signal type is reserved for framework infrastructure agents and
   105	the review-agent.
   106	
   107	See `agents.yaml` for the full schema and a commented-out example.
   108	Run `gestalt agents list <projectName>` to see the active agents
   109	for this project; `gestalt agents validate <projectName>` checks
   110	that your custom-agent definitions parse cleanly.
